![](viz/siri-b-i-d.png){width="20%" fig-align="center"}

The speaker replaces *Berlin* with *Dublin*, but Siri returns the weather for Berlin.
This is a **replacement self-repair (RSR)** [@shribergPreliminariesTheorySpeech1994].

::: {.notes}
Goal: the phenomenon is real and everyday. Name it only; the anatomy opens the Related Work section.
:::

## Current voice agents make the same mistake

Full-Duplex-Bench-v3 tests six spoken agents on real disfluent speech that requires API calls [@linFullDuplexBenchv3BenchmarkingTool2026].

| | The user says | The system fills in | The user wants |
|---|---|---|---|
| Siri | Berlin, I mean, Dublin | location = Berlin | Dublin |
| Gemini Live 3.1 | Rome, corrected to Milan | destination = Rome | Milan |

On self-corrections, the best system passes 58.8% of scenarios (GPT-Realtime) and the weakest 17.6%.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the second row is the Siri error in a current agent. The paper reports this as a case (the API is called before the correction ends), not as a rate; do not claim a proportion. TODO: verify the number of self-correction scenarios (the Pass@1 values are multiples of 1/17).
:::

## This talk asks two questions

1. **RQ1**: How can a meaning representation record a self-repair, keeping what was withdrawn, and what can it not cover?
2. **RQ2**: How well can LLM-based parsers learn this representation from synthesised data, and what errors remain?

&nbsp;

::: {.center}
Related Work → Pilot → **Representation** (RQ1) → Data → **Experiment Design** (RQ2)
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: the audience knows what the talk answers before any theory. Same substance as the RP RQs; "SBN" is replaced by "a meaning representation" because it has not been introduced yet. The roadmap row is the only roadmap; section slides later need one sentence each.
:::

# Related Work

## An RSR has three parts

> What is the weather like [in Berlin]~reparandum~, [I mean]~editing\ expression~, [in Dublin]~repair~?

- The **reparandum** is the material the speaker withdraws.
- The **editing expression** optionally signals the repair, e.g. *I mean*, *actually*, *no*.
- The **repair** is the material that replaces the reparandum.

This project covers replacements **within a single clause** [@leveltMonitoringSelfrepairSpeech1983; @shribergPreliminariesTheorySpeech1994].

## NLP pipelines either delete the reparandum or tag it

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
### Deletion
The reparandum and the editing expression are removed, and the fluent text is passed on [@johnsonTAGbasedNoisychannelModel2004].

→ *What is the weather like in Dublin?*
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
### Tagged transcription
The words are kept, and disfluent spans or tokens are labelled [@zayatsMultidomainDisfluencyRepair2014; @futamiStreamingJointSpeech2023].

→ *What is the weather like ~~in Berlin~~ in Dublin?*
:::
::::

Both approaches serve the same goal: recovering the speaker's final intention.

::: {.notes}
Goal: concede that this goal is right for task-oriented pipelines that only need the final request.
:::

## Deleted or tagged, the reparandum can still matter later

> What is the weather like in Berlin, I mean, in Dublin?
> Show me the airports of **these two cities**.

- After **deletion**, *these two cities* has only one antecedent left.
- After **tagging**, both names survive, but nothing records that Berlin was the location or that Dublin replaced it.

Psycholinguistic and dialogue studies show that the reparandum stays in the context [@lauLingeringEffectsDisfluent2005; @purverComputationalModelsMiscommunication2018].

::: {.notes}
Goal: first turning point of the talk.
:::

## A system needs three pieces of information about the revision

1. **Both candidates**: Berlin and Dublin
2. **Their status**: Berlin is withdrawn, Dublin is accepted
3. **The role they compete for**: the location in the weather request

All three concern what the utterance *means*, not which words were spoken.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the puzzle. Do not name the solution yet. These three items are reused as requirements (Representation); keep the wording identical.
:::

## A meaning representation is a graph of concepts and roles {.small-slide}

*What is the weather like in Dublin?*

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](viz/fluent_siri_example.svg){width="100%" fig-align="center"}
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
- **Nodes** are concepts: *weather*, *like*, a *city* named Dublin.
- **Edges** are roles: the city is the **Location** of the weather request.
- The **box** on the left is a context: it holds everything the speaker asserts.
:::
::::

Such a graph has room for all three pieces of information: two city nodes, a context for each, and one Location role. Because the structure is explicit, an output can be checked piece by piece.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the answer to the previous slide, with a picture (Michael). Argue inspectability, not performance; the thesis does not test downstream gains. If asked where MRs are used with LLMs: Backup table. The box is introduced here so that two boxes on the Representation slide need no explanation.
:::

## SBN writes this graph as text, so an LLM can generate it {.small-slide}

*What is the weather like in Dublin?*

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}
::: {.small}
```{.sbn code-line-numbers="false"}
entity.n.01 EQU ?                                   % What
time.n.08 EQU now                                   % is
weather.n.01                                        % the weather
like.a.01 Co-Theme -3 Time -2 Theme -1 Location +1  % like
city.n.01 Name "Dublin"                             % in Dublin?
```
:::
Each line introduces a concept. A role points to another concept by relative position: `-1` is the previous concept, `+1` the next.
:::
::: {.column width="36%"}
![](viz/fluent_siri_example.svg){fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

**Simplified Box Notation (SBN)** is the format of the Parallel Meaning Bank (PMB 5.1.0), which provides gold sentence–SBN pairs [@abzianidzeParallelMeaningBank2017; @bosSequenceNotationCatching2023]. Semantic parsing then becomes text-to-text: sentence in, SBN out.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the same graph as text; this is what the parser generates. Concepts are WordNet senses (weather.n.01 = first noun sense). SBN is an agreed notation; no linguistic backbone.
:::

# Pilot Study

## Can an existing SBN parser handle self-repair?

- **Parser**: Gemma-2 9B [@gemmateamGemma2Improving2024], fine-tuned with LoRA [@huLoRALowRankAdaptation2021] on fluent PMB pairs only.
- **Input**: 833 PMB sentences with an inserted reparandum, with and without *I mean* (2,499 each).
- **Correct answer**: the fluent gold SBN, i.e. the reparandum is left out [following @senSemanticParsingDisfluent2021].

| Fluent (PMB) | RSR, no editing expression | RSR + *I mean* |
|---|---|---|
| A cow gave birth to a calf with two heads. | **A goat**, a cow gave birth to a calf with two heads. | **A goat**, *I mean*, a cow gave birth to a calf with two heads. |

::: {.notes}
Goal: state exactly what the pilot does (Michael). The bar is deliberately low: only asks the parser to drop the reparandum, since fluent SBN cannot mark it as withdrawn. The 833 sentences come from PMB training data, so the parser had seen their fluent SBNs; only the RSR inputs were new. Reparanda: Qwen3-32B [@yangQwen3TechnicalReport2025], same part of speech, before one word.
:::

## Self-repair lowers parsing accuracy, and the parser asserts the reparandum

| Input | Scorable (%) | Failure-penalised F1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fluent | 97.5 | 0.950 |
| RSR, no editing expression | 94.6 | 0.786 |
| RSR + *I mean* | 76.5 | 0.609 |

- In **90.1%** of scorable RSR outputs the parse has *more* concepts than the fluent one: the goat is asserted, not dropped.
- A parse that asserts the goat still scores **0.764**: one graph score does not show whether the repair was handled.

::: {.smaller}
Scorable: the output converts into a graph. F1: SMATCH++ [@opitzSMATCHStandardizedExtended2023], unscorable outputs counted as 0.
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: numbers only (Michael); the analysis is in Backup (goat/cow DAGs, recognition probe, position effects). All pairwise F1 differences significant (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < .001). Median +2 concepts. The pilot shows the need for RSR supervision and for evaluation finer than SMATCH++; it does NOT show that SBN must be extended, that comes from later reference. The 0.764 pays off in Experiment Design.
:::

# Representation

## Keep both cities, and mark Berlin as withdrawn

*What is the weather like in Berlin, I mean, in Dublin?*

![](viz/siri_rsr_status.svg){width="100%" fig-align="center"}

| Both candidates | Their status | The role they compete for |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| two `city` nodes | a withdrawn and an accepted context | both are `LocationOf` the request |

::: {.notes}
Goal: the three pieces of information from Related Work, now visible in one graph; the table repeats the column heads of that slide word for word. Spoken, one sentence: SBN already has contexts whose content is represented but not asserted, e.g. negation (Backup: John did not buy a car). CORRECTION and CONJUNCTION are existing SBN separators; no new separator is introduced. CORRECTION follows SDRT's Correction relation (Backup). If pressed on data: CORRECTION does not occur in PMB 5.1.0 gold. Figure: render_status_graphs.py.
:::

## Both cities remain available for later reference; only Dublin is the requested location

> Show me the airports of **these two cities**.

![](viz/siri_later_reference.svg){width="100%" fig-align="center"}

*These two cities* links to both Berlin and Dublin (`ANA`), but Berlin does not become the requested location again.

::: {.smaller}
Berlin stays accessible because proper names project out of the withdrawn context [@bosVariablefreeDiscourseRepresentation2021]. The later-reference test set only uses referents that can project in this way.
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: close the loop opened in Related Work. The DAG carries the claim; one sentence states it, the small note states the mechanism and its limit. If the final DAG is too tall, switch to two columns (text left, DAG right).
:::

## The representation covers concept and role replacement; the corpus implements single concepts {.small-slide}

| | |
|---|---|
| **Representable** | Replacement of a concept or a role, also inside a context such as negation |
| **Implemented in the corpus** | Replacement of a single noun, verb or adjective concept |
| **Outside the design** | Replacement of a separator (e.g. *must* → *might*, *when* → *even though*); delayed repair |

::: {.notes}
Goal: keep "representable" and "implemented" apart; this is where the sharpest questions will land. Why not AMR or DS-TTR: Backup.
:::

# Data

## No corpus pairs self-repair with SBN, so PMB pairs are transformed on both sides {.small-slide}

The PMB has fluent sentence–SBN pairs; disfluency corpora have self-repairs but no SBN [@deshmukhResegmentationSWITCHBOARD1998; @passaliLARDLargescaleArtificial2022; @guptaDisflQABenchmarkDataset2021].

![](viz/paired_transformation.svg){width="70%" fig-align="center"}

Each item keeps the PMB split of its source document, so no training document reappears in evaluation.

::: {.notes}
Goal: why the data is generated, and how: both sides of a gold pair change together. Callback: the pilot changed only the input. The dashed "?" edge is what Experiment Design tests.
:::

## Steps ①–③: pick a concept, draw a competitor for it

<table>
<thead><tr><th>Step</th><th>Sentence side</th><th>SBN side</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>① Start from a gold PMB pair</td><td><em>What is the weather like in Dublin?</em></td><td>the SBN shown earlier</td></tr>
<tr class="fragment"><td>② Pick a noun, verb or adjective that a word expresses</td><td><em>weather</em></td><td><code>weather.n.01</code></td></tr>
<tr class="fragment"><td>③ Draw a WordNet sibling: same kind of thing, different value</td><td><em>storm</em></td><td><code>storm.n.01</code></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

::: {.fragment}
Other siblings of *weather* in the pool: *cloud*, *sunset*, *aurora*, *halo*, … Synonyms are never drawn, because the pool takes siblings only.
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: the audience follows one item through the pipeline; this slide and the next two are one continuous walkthrough. Step ② needs the word–concept alignment, which is why the step spans both sides. Siblings = WordNet co-hyponyms for nouns; verbs use VerbNet classes, adjectives FrameNet frames and antonyms. storm.n.01 is a real pool candidate for a PMB document with weather.n.01 (p99/d2202). Berlin → Dublin is not used here: proper names need an operator outside the implemented corpus.
Q&A: "How is storm found?" → Backup #/bk-wordnet. "Isn't a storm a kind of weather?" / "What about synonyms?" → Backup #/bk-synonyms.
:::

## Step ④: edit both sides of the pair together

*What is the weather like in Dublin?* → *What is **the storm**, I mean, the weather like in Dublin?*

::: {.small}
```{.sbn code-line-numbers="3-7"}
entity.n.01 EQU ?                                    % What
time.n.08 EQU now                                    % is
entity.n.01                                          % both fill this slot
    CORRECTION <1                                    % withdrawn:
storm.n.01 EQU -1                                    %   the storm
    CONJUNCTION <2                                   % accepted (I mean):
weather.n.01 EQU -2                                  %   the weather
like.a.01 Co-Theme -5 Time -4 Theme -3 Location +1   % like
city.n.01 Name "Dublin"                              % in Dublin?
```
:::

The same structure as Berlin and Dublin: a withdrawn context, an accepted context, one shared role (the Theme of *like*).

::: {.notes}
Goal: the pair is edited on both sides at once, so the target is known by construction; no parser is involved. Highlighted lines are what the generator adds; the indices of later concepts shift automatically. The shared entity.n.01 slot is the anchor construction, used when both candidates fill a role of a later concept (Backup: anchor and movement). The editing expression is optional: in training about 30% of items carry one. The SBN is the generator's output for this sentence; the sentence side is shown with "the" repeated, which is the natural form.
:::

## Step ⑤: keep only pairs that are well formed and make sense {.small-slide}

| Check | Rejects | Rejected example |
|---|---|---|
| **Structure** | ill-formed graph, wrong status, a missing link, any change outside the repair | — |
| **Contextual fit**: LM surprisal of the reparandum given its left context | a reparandum nobody would say | *cake → carburettor, for his wedding* |

The contextual-fit threshold is set on 150 hand-labelled candidates and frozen before the corpus is filtered.

::: {.notes}
Goal: why the corpus is not just random substitution. Status: the structural check is done over the whole training partition; contextual fit is being calibrated. Do not claim storm/weather passes the final filter: the threshold is not frozen yet.
Synonyms are not a filter here: they are excluded when the pool is built (Step ③, Backup #/bk-synonyms). NLI scores are computed and archived but reject nothing. The RP still describes an NLI filter; if Koller asks, the calibration sample showed the pool already contains almost no synonyms (1 of 150), so a synonym filter had nothing to do.
:::

## The training partition yields 16,425 candidate repair sites {.small-slide}

| PMB training partition (9,552 documents) | Count | % |
|---|---:|---:|
| Nouns, verbs and adjectives in the gold SBNs | 23,232 | 100.0 |
| … expressed by a word in the sentence | 17,886 | 77.0 |
| … with a WordNet competitor | 16,481 | 70.9 |
| … giving a well-formed repair-aware graph | 16,425 | 70.7 |

The transformation succeeds at 99.7% of the sites where a competitor exists. These sites are the candidate pool **before** linguistic filtering and sampling; the sampling rule is fixed before training.

::: {.notes}
Goal: known numbers only. Structural generation and validation are complete; linguistic filtering, the independent audit and final sampling remain. Most of the alignment loss is verbs without a surface word. 99.7% is the empirical side of RQ1's coverage question. Scope: immediate replacement of aligned noun, verb and adjective concepts in written PMB contexts; the experiments test learnability within these boundaries, not coverage of spontaneous RSR. The sampling rule limits repeated use of a source document.
:::

# Experiment Design

## Three training conditions: same inputs, different targets {.small-slide}

Training input: *What is the storm, I mean, the weather like in Dublin?*

| Condition | Role | Target for this input | Answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fluent only | **reference**: the pilot parser | — (never sees RSR input) | how far a parser gets without RSR training |
| RSR normalisation | **baseline**: deletion | the fluent SBN: *weather* only | what keeping the reparandum buys and costs |
| Repair-aware | **this project** | *storm* withdrawn, *weather* accepted | RQ2: can the representation be learned? |

The controlled comparison is between the **baseline** and **repair-aware** conditions: they share inputs, example counts and training, and only the target differs.

::: {.smaller}
Qwen3.5 at 2B, 9B and 27B [@qwenQwen35Native2026] is fine-tuned with LoRA under all three conditions, with three seeds each (27 runs). One parsing instruction serves all conditions and does not say whether an input contains a repair.
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: pre-empt the CS reflex that the most vanilla setting is the baseline. Fluent only vs repair-aware changes both the examples and the targets, so it is a reference, not the controlled comparison. All conditions keep the same fluent PMB pairs. Three sizes so the target effect can be compared across model capacities. Qwen3.5 because it is the most recent family with dense checkpoints across the sizes needed. Normalisation is an end-to-end parser, not a pipeline.
:::

## A single graph score cannot tell opposite failures apart

Test input: *What is the storm, I mean, the weather like in Dublin?*

| Output | Typical of | SMATCH++ |
|---|---|---:|
| *storm* dropped | baseline | 0.67 |
| *storm* asserted as well | reference | 0.68 |
| *storm* withdrawn, *weather* accepted | repair-aware | 1.00 |

The first two outputs are wrong in opposite ways: one loses the storm, the other asserts it. [Yet their scores are almost the same]{.fg}, just as the pilot's goat parse still scored 0.764.

::: {.smaller}
Constructed outputs, scored against the repair-aware gold graph with the project's evaluator.
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: the problem before the solution. These are hand-built outputs standing for each condition's typical behaviour, not model predictions (storm_weather_scores.md). Exact: 0.667 / 0.680 / 1.000. A pilot-style output that also turns "I mean" into an event scores 0.557; not shown, the goat/cow DAGs in Backup cover that case.
:::

## Two measures tell them apart {.small-slide}

| Output | SMATCH++ | RSR-structure accuracy | Accepted meaning |
|---|---:|:-:|---:|
| *storm* dropped | 0.67 | ✗ | 1.00 |
| *storm* asserted as well | 0.68 | ✗ | 0.95 |
| *storm* withdrawn, *weather* accepted | 1.00 | ✓ | 1.00 |

- **RSR-structure accuracy** (primary): both candidates, correct status, the shared role. → *Can the representation be learned?*
- **Accepted meaning**: remove the withdrawn part, compare with the fluent graph. → *Does keeping the reparandum cost the final request?*
- **Later reference** (Berlin/Dublin test set): can *these two cities* reach both? → *What does keeping it buy?*

::: {.notes}
Goal: each measure answers one part of RQ2. RSR-structure accuracy is read in absolute terms: only the repair-aware parser is trained on the structure, so it is expected to lead. Accepted meaning compares baseline and repair-aware; its job is the cost, not catching the reference parser; if asked about the 0.95, that is why it cannot be the primary measure. Also reported: SMATCH++ and the spurious-RSR rate on the unmodified PMB test set. Full matrix: Backup.
:::

## Further tests check that the parser learned the distinction, not a surface cue {.small-slide}

| Possible shortcut | Test | Example |
|---|---|---|
| The editing expression triggers the structure | Each test item with and without one; *sorry* never appears in training | *What is the storm, **sorry**, the weather like in Dublin?* |
| Any two adjacent words of the same kind trigger it | Lists, appositions and coordination without replacement | *We flew to Berlin, Dublin and Paris.* (no repair) |
| The structure is applied beyond one clause | Corrections across turns | A: *Is it Berlin?* B: *No, Dublin.* |

About 30% of repair training inputs carry *I mean*, *no*, *no wait* or *actually*; the rest carry none.

::: {.notes}
Goal: answer the obvious objection to synthetic data before it is raised. The non-RSR documents are held out of training (9,447 training documents remain). The examples in the third column are illustrations of each test type, not items from the test sets. Error categories: Backup.
:::

## Summary: keep both cities, mark the withdrawn one {.small-slide}

| | |
|----|------------|
| **Related Work** | Deletion loses Berlin; tagging keeps it but not its status or its role. |
| **Pilot** | A parser trained on fluent SBN often asserts the reparandum, and SMATCH++ hides the error. |
| **Representation** | A withdrawn and an accepted context (`CORRECTION`, `CONJUNCTION`) record both candidates, their status and the role they compete for. |
| **Data** | Editing PMB pairs on both sides yields 16,425 candidate sites; the transformation succeeds at 99.7% of them. |
| **Experiment Design** *(planned)* | Three conditions at three model sizes test whether the structure is learnable, and what keeping the reparandum buys and costs. |

Back to Siri: a parser that produces this representation queries the weather in Dublin, and can still resolve *these two cities* to Berlin and Dublin.

::: {.notes}
Goal: one sentence per roadmap section, in the same words as the section's key slide, so the chain can be reread here. Only the first four rows are findings; Experiment Design is the plan. Close on Siri: the accepted meaning gives the right API call, the kept reparandum serves later reference.
:::

## Pilot: Full Results and Position Effects

## Recognition Probe: the failure is not only a failure to notice the repair

The base Gemma-2 9B, without the adapter, was asked to mark the reparandum, the editing expression and the repair in plain text.

| Input | RSR detected (%) |
|---|---:|
| Fluent (false alarm) | 1.0 |
| RSR, no editing expression | 44.8 |
| RSR + *I mean* | 100.0 |

With *I mean*, the base model notices every repair, yet the fine-tuned parser often represents *I mean* as content. Without it, the base model misses more than half.

::: {.notes}
Goal: pre-empt "the parser just didn't notice the repair". State the limit before anyone asks: the probe changes the task and removes the adapter, so it cannot isolate SBN generation as the error source. The gap with and without an editing expression motivates the paired test items in Data. Span F1 and position breakdown go to Backup.
:::

## Goat/Cow: the parser asserts the reparandum and turns *I mean* into an event

*A goat, I mean, a cow gave birth to a calf with two heads.*

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Fluent reference**

![](viz/goat_cow_fluent.svg){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Parse of the RSR input**

![](viz/goat_cow_rsr_parse.svg){width="100%"}
:::
::::

Most of the graph matches the reference, so the parse still scores **0.764** SMATCH++. Nothing in it records that the cow replaces the goat.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the DAGs replace the SBN strings (strings on the next slide). The picture explains the 0.764: a correct graph with extra structure grown onto it.
:::

## Goat/Cow: SBN Strings

*A goat, I mean, a cow gave birth to a calf with two heads.*

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
Fluent reference
```{.sbn code-line-numbers="false"}
cow.n.01                                     % cow
give_birth.v.01 Agent -1 Time +1 Patient +2  % gave birth
time.n.08 TPR now
calf.n.01 Part +2                            % calf
quantity.n.01 EQU 2                          % two
head.n.01 Quantity -1                        % heads
```
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
Parse of the RSR input
```{.sbn code-line-numbers="false"}
goat.n.01                                    % goat
person.n.01 EQU speaker                      % I
mean.v.01 Theme -2 Agent -1 Time +1          % mean
time.n.08 EQU now
cow.n.01                                     % cow
give_birth.v.01 Agent -1 Time +1 Patient +2  % gave birth
time.n.08 TPR now
calf.n.01 Part +2                            % calf
quantity.n.01 EQU 2                          % two
head.n.01 Quantity -1                        % heads
```
:::
::::

## No current approach records the revision in the meaning

| | Both candidates | Their status | The role they compete for |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Deletion | ✗ | — | — |
| Tagged transcription | ✓ | ✓ (on words) | ✗ |
| Parser trained on fluent SBN (pilot) | ✓^a^ | ✗ | ✗ |
| **This project** | ✓ | ✓ (in the meaning) | ✓ |

::: {.smaller}
^a^ 90.1% of scorable outputs contain more concepts than the fluent parse; the reparandum is often kept as asserted content.
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: the columns are the three pieces of information from Related Work; the table needs no example to be read.
:::

## SBN can already keep content without asserting it: contexts

*John did not buy a car.*

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.small}
```{.sbn code-line-numbers="false"}
male.n.02 Name "John"               % John
    NEGATION <1                     % did not
time.n.08 TPR now
buy.v.01 Agent -2 Time -1 Theme +1  % buy
car.n.01                            % a car
```
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](viz/negation_john.svg){.nostretch width="100%" fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

- A **separator** such as `NEGATION` opens a new **context**: the buying event and the car are represented, but their content is denied.
- **Accessibility**: a link may reach out of the negated context (to John), but not into it.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the first piece of information (keep the reparandum without asserting it) needs exactly this device.
:::

## `CORRECTION` holds the withdrawn candidate, `CONJUNCTION` the accepted one {.small-slide}

```{.sbn code-line-numbers="false"}
entity.n.01 EQU ?                       % What
time.n.08 EQU now                       % is
weather.n.01                            % the weather
like.a.01 Co-Theme -3 Time -2 Theme -1  % like
    CORRECTION <1
city.n.01 Name "Berlin" LocationOf -1   % in Berlin
    CONJUNCTION <2                      % I mean,
city.n.01 Name "Dublin" LocationOf -2   % in Dublin?
```

- `CORRECTION` opens the context for Berlin. Following SDRT's *Correction* relation, its content is withdrawn: ¬K~π1~ ∧ K~π2~ [@lascaridesAgreementDisputesCommitments2009].
- `CONJUNCTION` opens the context for Dublin and merges it back into the shared request.
- Both cities link to the weather request with `LocationOf`, so the revised role is recorded.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the three pieces of information, met one per bullet. RP wording: the representation pairs the existing separators CORRECTION and CONJUNCTION and introduces no new separator. If pressed on data: CORRECTION does not occur in PMB 5.1.0 gold.
:::

## Abstract Description

:::{.text-center}

$$
K = K_{\pi_{\text{pre}}} \land \neg K_{\pi_m} \land \big(K_{\pi_n} \land K_{\pi_{\text{post}}}\big) \land \varphi_{\mathit{Corr}(\pi_m,\pi_n)}
$$
:::

where:
$K_{\pi_m}$ represents the reparandum
$K_{\pi_n}$ represents the repair
$K_{\pi_{\text{post}}}$ represents the continuation after the repair

## Why Not AMR or DS-TTR

Why SBN rather than AMR [@banarescuAbstractMeaningRepresentation2013] or DS-TTR [@houghProcessingSelfrepairsIncremental2012]: AMR lacks separate semantic contexts and does not record the order of the replacement; DS-TTR keeps the withdrawn path only in its processing history. SBN separates contexts, and the PMB supplies sentence–SBN pairs.

## Each item edits a gold pair on both sides, then checks both sides

![](viz/data_pipeline.svg){width="100%" fig-align="center"}

::: {.smaller}
Running example: the Siri request. The reparandum and the SBN splice are the generator's output for this sentence. Dashed: in progress.
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: the intuition of data synthesis in one picture. Top lane = sentence, bottom lane = SBN, as in the previous square. Steps ② and ③ span both lanes because the word–concept alignment ties a word to a concept. Step ④ is where the two sides are edited in parallel; "linked to shared content" covers the direct, anchor and movement constructions (this example uses the anchor construction; see Backup). The step names match the rows of the yield table. Berlin → Dublin is NOT used here: proper names need a separate operator that is not part of the implemented corpus.
The utterance is shown with "the" repeated (the natural form); the generator currently may also repeat "is", a data issue to fix before the data is frozen.
:::

## One generated record keeps the source, every choice made and both sides of the new pair {#bk-record}

::: {.small}
```{.yaml code-line-numbers="false"}
# PMB source
doc_id:             p42/d1468
split:              train
nl_clean:           Let's sit in the shade.
sbn_clean: >
  time.n.08 TSU now person.n.01 EQU speaker
  sit.v.01 Time -2 Theme -1 Location +1 shade.n.01
# Repair selection and transformation
# the third concept in the sequence, counted from zero
concept_pos:        2
repair_synset:      sit.v.01
reparandum_synset:  stand.v.01
reparandum_surface: stand
strategy:           inplace
devices:            d1_drop_role
blockers:           —
# the largest role index without its sign; the ceiling is nine
max_abs_index:      3
# Generated pair
nl_repair:          Let's stand, sit in the shade.
nl_repair_interr:   Let's stand, I mean, sit in the shade.
sbn_repair: >
  time.n.08 TSU now person.n.01 EQU speaker
  CORRECTION <1 stand.v.01 Time -2 Theme -1
  CONJUNCTION <2 sit.v.01 Time -3 Theme -2 Location +1 shade.n.01
# Validation (NLI scores are archived, not used for filtering)
# 1 = well-formed graph; items with 0 are dropped
legal:              1
entail_fwd:         0.0005
entail_bwd:         0.0005
synonymy:           0.0005
```
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: answer "what does one finished item look like?". Source: RP Appendix "Example Generated Corpus Record" (tab:worked-record), fields and values unchanged, shown as the record itself (YAML) rather than a table; the RP groups are the comment lines. This is a real record for a verb site (in-place construction), unlike storm/weather in the main deck, which uses the anchor construction.
The last group's comment differs from the RP heading ("Validation and filtering"): the NLI scores are archived and filter nothing (see #/bk-synonyms). A transformation that exceeds the single-digit index ceiling is recorded as legal 0 with index_overflow among its blockers.
:::

## Noun competitors are WordNet siblings: one step up, then all children {#bk-wordnet}

![](viz/wordnet_siblings.svg){width="100%" fig-align="center"}

For a noun, the generator goes one step up from the repair concept and takes the parent's other children as candidates. This is how *storm* is found for *weather*, together with *cloud*, *sunset* and the rest.

::: {.smaller}
Verbs and adjectives follow the same idea by other routes: VerbNet class-mates for verbs, FrameNet frame-mates and antonyms for adjectives. In each case the candidate fills the same slot with a different value.
:::

::: {.notes}
Goal: answer "how is storm found?". Rule: repair_data_gen/wn_candidates.py `_cohyponyms`. Figure: render_wordnet_siblings.py (reads the sibling list from WordNet). atmospheric_phenomenon.n.01 has 16 children. Next slide answers the follow-up about synonyms.
:::

## Synonyms never enter the pool, and *storm* is a more specific word, not a synonym {#bk-synonyms .small-slide}

- The pool draws siblings only. WordNet's near-synonym relations (`similar_to` clusters, verb groups) are never used, and a candidate that shares a lemma with the repair is dropped. *Couch → sofa* cannot occur: *couch* and *sofa* are lemmas of one synset.
- In a hand-labelled sample of 150 candidates, annotators judged only **1** to mean the same as the repair.
- *Storm* is more specific than *weather*: an NLI model [@laurerLessAnnotatingMore2024] finds entailment in one direction only (*storm* ⇒ *weather* 0.84; *weather* ⇒ *storm* 0.005). Moving from a too-specific word to a more general one is a natural repair.

::: {.notes}
Goal: answer "isn't a storm a kind of weather?" and "what about synonyms?". WordNet places storm as a sibling of weather although its gloss reads "a violent weather condition": the tree and the gloss disagree, which is why the NLI score is shown as a diagnostic.
If asked how much NLI filters: nothing. NLI scores are computed and archived for possible later use; the synonym class is empty by construction (pool stage), so a threshold would only remove good candidates. The RP still describes an NLI filter; this is the change since the RP.
Why not embedding similarity: it scores hot/cold as similar as sofa/couch, so it cannot separate "interchangeable" from "different values on one dimension".
:::

## Anchor and Movement Constructions

- **Anchor**: *Josh, I mean, Mary bought a cake*: shared `entity.n.01`, both candidates `EQU` it
- **Movement**: *Tom opened, no, broke the window*: *window* moved before the paired contexts

::: {.notes}
Goal: operational conventions for sites where the direct construction fails. Show only if asked; full listings from RP Appendix.
:::

## RSR-structure accuracy shows learnability; the two RSR conditions show benefit and cost {.small-slide}

| Question | Comparison | Measure | Test data |
|---|---|---|---|
| Can the representation be learned? | repair-aware, absolute | RSR-structure accuracy, error types | generated RSR test items |
| What does keeping the reparandum buy? | normalisation vs repair-aware | links to the withdrawn referent | later-reference challenge set |
| What does it cost? | normalisation vs repair-aware | accepted meaning | generated RSR test items |
| | all conditions | SMATCH++, spurious-RSR rate | unmodified PMB test set |

RSR-structure accuracy, the primary measure, is read in absolute terms: the repair-aware parser is expected to lead the other conditions on it, since only it is trained on that structure.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the full evaluation matrix. The design sets no threshold for declaring the richer representation cost-free; paired differences show the size of any cost.
:::

## Error Categories

Errors are classified as missing configuration, reversed status, wrong link to shared content, reparandum left in accepted content, editing expression represented as content, spurious RSR, or malformed SBN.

::: {.notes}
Goal: the error categories are fixed before the test outputs are inspected.
:::

## Statistics {.small-slide}

- **Unit of observation**: the PMB source document; all variants of a source are averaged before comparison.
- **Seeds**: for each model size and matched seed, paired document-level differences with 95% confidence intervals from 10,000 paired bootstrap samples; within each size, the mean and range of the three differences summarise training variation. A result counts as stable only when all three differences have the same direction.
- **Multiple comparisons**: Holm correction within each family of secondary comparisons.

::: {.notes}
Goal: RP Appendix "Statistical Comparisons". Show only if asked.
:::
